correctness.rationale: The exact circle Fourier integral reduces every real polynomial through degree 3 to signed winding relations. Linear/diagonal quadratic moments enforce positive nonzero distinct winding absolute values and equal amplitudes; cubic moments vanish iff the positive absolute spectrum is sum-free with repetitions. Reflection around each prefix maximum yields a_j>=2j-1 for all j; squared speed gives exact length and forces the unique odd spectrum at equality. The fourth moment is incompatible for all d>1. The embedded exact checker tests 39304 signed primitive small winding vectors and independent finite sum-free bounds; the infinite proof is the analytic reflection argument.

value.rationale: The 2026 King–Mixon global shortest spherical 3-design candidate is the symmetric moment curve, known but conjectural in the unrestricted class. A full sharp classification and unique exact length minimizer among ALL primitive one-parameter diagonal-unitary orbits is natural rigorously proven partial progress, with phase-only mobile quadrature interpretation. It identifies precisely which windings integrate cubic moments and proves the optimal exact acquisition length in this canonical torus-orbit class. Neither the existence nor global conjectured shortest status of the odd curve is claimed as new.
